summary: Olga Coal Company tower site in McDowell County, listed as gone. The record gives a 1939 first day in service; no present-day description found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source read describes what remains at the site.
facts.agency: Alawest (administrator per the Former Fire Lookout Sites record)

events.note: First day in service, October 12, 1939, per the Former Fire Lookout Sites record; not a construction date
Company sold to a group of industrialists who renamed it the Olga Coal Company, per Wikipedia; company-level, not a tower event
April 18, 1986 Bluefield Daily Telegraph report, quoted on Forest Lookouts: 40-foot tower on Olga Coal Company property; names only the Olga Fire Tower and is not tied to No. 1 with certainty

evidence.supports: Olga Coal Company built the tower
evidence.quote: This tower was originally built by Olga Coal Company.

evidence.supports: Elevation of the site, 2,458 ft (749 m)
Olga Coal Company name dates from a 1947 sale and rename
evidence.quote: Carter died in 1936, and the company was then taken over by his son James who sold it in 1947 to a group of industrialists who changed the company name to the Olga Coal Company.

evidence.supports: 1986 report: 40-foot tower on Olga Coal Company property
evidence.quote: The 40-foot tower is on property owned by the Olga Coal Company.

evidence.supports: 1986 report: Department of Agriculture maintains the tower and cabin
evidence.quote: The Department of Agriculture maintains the tower and the small cabin.

evidence.supports: 1986 report: observer in charge for five years; tower named only as the Olga Fire Tower
evidence.quote: has been in charge of the Olga Fire Tower for five years
Olga No. 1 McDowell 37.36499 -81.68584 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1675, WV 66

notes_for_editor: The FFLOS record gives October 12, 1939 as the first day in service, not a construction year, and no build year was found. Wikipedia's Coalwood article dates the Olga Coal Company name from a 1947 sale and rename, eight years after the 1939 date. The sources read do not say whether that is the same company, so the story reports the gap without resolving it. The 1986 Bluefield Daily Telegraph report, quoted on Forest Lookouts, names only the Olga Fire Tower and is not treated as a fact about No. 1; the same caveat is in us-wv-olga-no-2. No access or present-day site information was found. Wikipedia is used as a lead only; its own citations were not checked. The brief's coordinates, elevation and status agree with the sources; no corrections proposed.
